name: Mieliebrood
summary: Sweetcorn bread: a moist, golden loaf packed with creamed sweetcorn, baked in a loaf tin and sliced warm with butter, alongside a braai or a bowl of soup.
about: Mieliebrood (mielie bread) belongs to the Afrikaans farm kitchen, where it was traditionally made from freshly grated green mielies and steamed in a covered tin over a pot of boiling water. Today most home cooks bake it with tinned creamed sweetcorn. It goes to the braai as a side, and leftover slices are toasted for breakfast.

ingredients.name: Butter
ingredients.note: melted and cooled, plus extra for the tin

steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C (160 °C fan). Grease a 22 × 11 cm loaf tin with butter and line the base with baking paper.
Sift the flour, baking powder and salt into a large bowl and stir in the sugar.
In another bowl whisk the eggs, milk and melted butter together, then stir in the creamed sweetcorn.
Pour the wet mixture into the dry ingredients and fold together with a spoon until just combined with no dry flour showing. Do not overmix; the batter will be thick and slightly lumpy.
Spoon the batter into the tin, level the top and bake for 50 to 60 minutes, until risen and golden brown and a skewer pushed into the centre comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a rack. Slice thickly and serve warm with butter.
prepNote: Keeps 2 days wrapped at room temperature; toast or warm slices before serving.
